data.description: Path to data relative to project data folder.  A layer within a geopackage may be selected by appending its name after a colon, and those features may then optionally be filtered, for example "region_boundaries/your_geopackage.gpkg:layer_name -where \"SOME_ATTRIBUTE='some value'\"".  Alternatively, features may be selected from the imported OpenStreetMap polygons using the syntax "OSM:some_tag is not NULL".

id.description: The field used as a unique identifier (default: ogc_fid)

keep_columns.description: A list of column field names to be retained.  Columns retained here are also available as weights when this aggregation is itself used as an aggregation source.

aggregation_source.description: The indicator layer to be aggregated: "point" (sample points), "grid" (the population grid), or the name of another custom aggregation.  Aggregations are processed in the order they are configured, so an aggregation named as a source must be defined before the one that summarises it; a source that has not yet been processed cannot be identified and is skipped.

weight.description: The variable used for weighting, matched case insensitively (column names are lower cased when data are imported).  Where the aggregation source is areal (the population grid, or an earlier custom aggregation) and carries this column, it is summed across the units falling within each boundary to give that boundary's total, and indicator estimates are weighted by it.  Where the source is sample points, the weight is instead read from the aggregation boundaries themselves, because sample points are equal probability samples of the network and summing a boundary attribute once per point would multiply it; the boundary value is reported as the population estimate, but indicator estimates are unweighted.  Leave blank or set to false for no weighting.  A weight that cannot be located produces a warning naming the tables searched, and does not halt analysis.

aggregate_within_distance.description: Optional distance in metres within which units of the aggregation source are to be summarised for each boundary, instead of the default of summarising those which intersect it.  Catchments defined in this way may overlap and need not intersect the units they summarise, so area apportionment of weights is not applied.

clip.description: Whether the aggregation boundaries are restricted to the urban study region, which defines the analytical area of this study region (default: true).  Where true, the geometry and area reported in the resulting 'indicators_' table describe the part of each boundary that was actually analysed, and the boundaries as configured are retained unchanged in the corresponding 'agg_' table, so that the two may be overlaid to see what each area did and did not contribute.  Set to false to summarise and report the configured boundaries in full.

area_weighted.description: Whether to apportion weighted grid cells by the share of their area falling within each aggregation boundary, so that cells straddling a boundary are divided between the areas they span rather than counted in full in each (default: true).  Only applies where the aggregation source is the population grid, a weight is defined, and aggregate_within_distance is not used.

sampling.description: Optional configuration of sample point generation, allowing analysis of areas lacking population data coverage

sample_unpopulated_areas.description: Set to true to generate sample points along the network throughout the urban study region regardless of population data coverage, or provide a path to a polygon layer (relative to the project data folder) to restrict additional sampling to specific areas of interest (e.g. new developments post-dating a population census).  Sample points lacking population coverage are excluded from population-weighted grid and city summaries, but are included in custom aggregations.

custom_sample_points.description: Optional path to a point layer (relative to the project data folder) of custom sample point locations to be analysed in addition to those generated along the network.  Points are associated with the nearest network edge within the configured snap tolerance.

custom_sample_points_snap_tolerance.description: Maximum distance in metres from the network within which custom sample points will be associated with their nearest edge (default: 500).

points_of_interest.description: Optional custom points of interest, supplementing or replacing the destinations identified using OpenStreetMap.  Each entry is named using a destination category (dest_name), for example 'fresh_food_market', 'convenience' or 'pt_any' as listed under 'Destinations' in configuration/indicators.yml, or another category defined in configuration/osm_destination_definitions.csv.  A category that is not listed in indicators.yml will be imported and mapped, but will not have an access indicator calculated for it unless indicators.yml is also extended to include it.  A category may be configured as a single data entry, as a mapping carrying a category-level 'replace' setting and a 'data_sources' list of entries pooled within that category, or as a bare list of entries.  Note that the project configuration (configuration/config.yml) also defines a 'points_of_interest' setting recording the OpenStreetMap destination definitions used for all regions; that setting is unrelated to this one.

data.description: Path to a spatial data file relative to the project data directory.  Data are reprojected to the study region coordinate reference system automatically, and point centroids are recorded as destinations.  A layer within a geopackage may be selected by appending its name after a colon, and features may then optionally be filtered, for example "other_custom_data/your_geopackage.gpkg:layer_name -where \"SOME_ATTRIBUTE='some value'\"".

data_sources.description: List of data entries pooled within this category (category-level form; use together with a single category-level 'replace' setting instead of 'data')

replace.description: Set to true to use these data instead of OpenStreetMap for this destination category, skipping the OpenStreetMap import for it entirely.  The default (false) pools these features with those identified using OpenStreetMap, which is appropriate for the distance to closest destination analyses undertaken.  Where multiple data sources are configured for a category they must agree on this setting; custom data sources never replace one another.

dest_name_full.description: Optional plain language name for this destination category, required only where the category is not one defined in configuration/osm_destination_definitions.csv (otherwise it is looked up; the fallback is the category name itself)

domain.description: Optional domain for this destination category, required only where the category is not one defined in configuration/osm_destination_definitions.csv (otherwise it is looked up; the fallback is 'Custom')

keep_columns.description: Optional source data columns to retain for each imported destination, given as a list or a comma-separated string.  Their values are stored as destination tags, so that a category imported once may later be subdivided using SQL on its source classification (for example "tags->>'codigo_act' IN ('461121','461130')") wherever a destination filter is accepted, rather than by declaring further near-duplicate entries.  Columns not present in the source data are reported and skipped.

source.description: The source of this destination data

url.description: The URL from where it was downloaded

data.description: Path relative to the project data directory (optionally with '-where "..."' filter or ':layer' suffix)

url.description: The URL from where it was downloaded

replace.description: Replace the OpenStreetMap-derived data for this category (must be consistent across the category's entries; default false: supplement)

areas_of_interest.description: Optional areas of interest configuration. 'public_open_space' supplies custom area data (a mapping with a category-level 'replace' setting and a 'data_sources' list, a bare list of entries, or a single data entry). 'osm_open_space' is a distinct, optional entry overriding individual OpenStreetMap open space definitions for this region, so locally-relevant open space typologies can be captured without pre-processing custom data.

osm_open_space.description: Region-specific overrides of the open space definitions in configuration/osm_open_space.yml. Any definition not listed keeps its global default; a definition that is listed has its 'criteria' replaced outright (given directly as a string or list, or as a mapping containing a 'criteria' key so a whole block may be copied and edited). Valid definition names: additional_public_criteria, identifying_tags_to_exclude_other_than_name, linear_feature_criteria, os_add_as_tags, os_boundary, os_excluded_keys, os_excluded_values, os_inclusion, os_landuse, os_linear, os_required, os_water, os_water_sports, public_not_in. Derived criteria (public_space, exclusion_criteria) are recomposed from their sources and cannot be overridden. Has no effect where public_open_space is configured with 'replace: true'.

public_open_space.description: Optional custom public open space data, used instead of the areas of public open space that are otherwise derived from OpenStreetMap using the tag definitions in configuration/osm_open_space.yml.  The supplied polygons are taken to be the public open space of the study region in their entirety, and their areas are used for the 'any' and 'large' (over 1.5 hectares) open space access indicators; they should therefore already be restricted to those areas considered publicly accessible.  If no features are retrieved for the study region, analysis halts with an error rather than proceeding as though the region had no open space.

data.description: Path to a polygon data file relative to the project data directory.  A layer within a geopackage may be selected by appending its name after a colon, and features may then optionally be filtered, for example "other_custom_data/your_geopackage.gpkg:open_space -where \"ACCESS='public'\""; the filter syntax may also be used on its own with other formats, for example "other_custom_data/your_open_space.shp -where \"ACCESS='public'\"".

source.description: The source of the public open space data

url.description: The URL from where it was downloaded

gee.description: Set to true to additionally compute the optional Google Earth Engine indicators: Large Public Urban Green Space (LPUGS) accessibility and availability, and the Global Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (GUHVI).  This requires the software to have been launched using the Earth Engine container (global-indicators-ee.bat or global-indicators-ee.sh) along with a Google Cloud project registered for Earth Engine; where Earth Engine is unavailable, a message is displayed and analysis proceeds without these indicators.  The 'spatial_ee' and 'policy_spatial_ee' reporting templates are used to include them in generated reports.  Default: false.

policy_review.description: Optional path to include policy indicator checklist in generated reports

routing_engine.description: Accessibility routing engine for the pedestrian neighbourhood analysis (nearest-POI distances and the neighbourhood density all-pairs search) and, unless overridden by cycling_indicators.routing_engine, the cycling analysis including its activity-centre walk-sheds: 'pgrouting' (default; batched pgr_drivingDistance in PostGIS, with networkx for the density search) or 'inmemory' (exact in-process Dijkstra; identical results, far faster on large cities and light on RAM).
